Optimal.Notes: The 40 Hz refresh and frame cap delivers a smooth, judder-free experience that suits the game's paced driving; medium shadows and high textures give a great-looking cab and road environment without taxing the GPU. This is the recommended daily-driver profile.

profiles.Summary: Euro Truck Simulator 2 is a well-optimised, older simulation title that runs comfortably on the Steam Deck, with the RDNA 2 GPU easily handling its graphical demands at native resolution. The game is Steam Deck Verified and plays smoothly under Proton with no major compatibility hurdles reported.
profiles.BasisNote: No specific Steam Deck player reports were available; profiles are estimated from the PC minimum/recommended requirements (GTX 660–GTX 1660 target), the game's age and engine efficiency, and the Deck's RDNA 2 GPU capability. On your first run, check frame rates in a busy city or motorway junction — if you see consistent dips below your cap, lower Shadow Quality and Rendering Distance first.

MaxBattery.Notes: Dropping render resolution and capping TDP to 6 W keeps the APU very cool and extends battery life significantly; the game's slow-paced nature makes 30 fps feel natural. FSR upscaling from 960x600 recovers sharpness with minimal visual cost.

KnownIssues: Controller/gamepad input may need in-game calibration as the game was designed primarily for keyboard and mouse; a steering wheel profile may need manual binding.
Text and UI elements can be small at 1280x800 — increasing UI scale in the game's settings is recommended.
Online multiplayer (TruckersMP) requires a separate launcher and may not work natively under Proton without extra steps.
Mods from the Steam Workshop may occasionally cause instability or require revalidation after game updates.

MaxPerformance.Notes: The Deck's GPU handles ETS2 at native 1280x800 with high/ultra settings comfortably in open roads, though dense cities and busy motorways may dip to the low 50s; clamping the frame limit to 60 prevents wasted power chasing uncapped frames. Battery life is short at full TDP, so plug in or drop to Optimal for portable sessions.

Optimal.Notes: The locked 40 fps at 40 Hz gives perfectly smooth trucking; FSR upscaling from 1024x640 keeps the image sharp enough while the 10 W TDP handles busy city traffic without stutter.

profiles.Summary: Euro Truck Simulator 2 is a well-optimised, older simulation title that runs natively well on the Steam Deck via Proton, with the RDNA 2 GPU comfortably exceeding its minimum and approaching its recommended GPU spec. The game is largely CPU-bound at higher settings and scales gracefully down to low TDP, making it an excellent fit for long handheld sessions.

On your first run, check frame pacing in a busy city like Paris or Berlin — if fps dips below your cap, lower Shadow Quality and Rendering Distance first, as these are the heaviest settings in ETS2.

MaxBattery.Notes: Rendering at 960x600 with FSR upscaling keeps the GPU load very low; the 6 W TDP cap is sufficient for highway driving but may cause brief dips to 28 fps in dense city centres.

Steam Input may require manual controller mapping configuration for full button prompts.
Some DLC truck interiors with high-res textures can cause occasional frame dips in busy city areas.
The game's launcher may appear on first run; dismiss it and launch the game directly thereafter.

MaxPerformance.Notes: Native 1280x800 at high/ultra settings is achievable on open highways but expect dips to 45 fps in large cities with many parked vehicles and traffic; the 15 W TDP cap is required to sustain this.
